title: Integrated Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement & Revenue Recognition (FY2026)
author: Daniel Park
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard procedures for annual budgeting and quarterly forecasting, contract intake and review, procurement approvals, and revenue recognition / billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement coordinators, and product & sales leaders who manage commitments and customer contracts.

Scope:
- Budget owners (Product, Eng, GTM) and Finance planning team
- Commercial contracts (MSA, SOW, Order Forms), procurement of third-party services, and vendor onboarding
- Revenue accounting for Hosted API (usage-based), Dedicated reservations (committed capacity), and Private deployments (license + services)

Quick links (templates & systems):
- Budget template (Google Sheet): /drive/redwood/finance/budgets/FY2026-budget-template
- Contract intake form: /forms/contract-intake
- Vendor risk assessment (VRA): /tools/vra
- Contract repository (DocStore): docstore.redwood.com/contracts
- Billing system: bill.redwood.com / Accounting ERP: NetLedger

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (annual & rolling):
Purpose: Produce an accurate, driver-based headcount and expense plan to support product roadmaps and capacity commitments while preserving runway targets.
Cadence and owner:
- Annual budget (owner: Finance FP&A lead) 
  - Kickoff: Nov (prior FY)
  - Final approval: Board-submitted by Feb 15
- Quarterly rolling forecast (owner: FP&A + GTM FP lead)
  - Forecast windows: Q-end + 10 business days
  - Re-forecast triggers: >15% variance to plan or material product roadmap changes

Process (high level):
1. Budget Kickoff: Finance circulates template, assumptions and top-down revenue targets.
2. Department submissions: Each budget owner submits headcount, opex, and capital requests with supporting rationale and feature priority (template required).
3. Investment review: Finance + Product + Eng leadership score and prioritize requests against strategic themes.
4. Consolidation & scenario analysis: FP&A models best/worst cases, cash runway sensitivity, and unit-economics impact (CAC payback, gross margin on Hosted API).
5. Leadership review & finalization: CEO & CFO sign-off; Board packet prepared.

Budget artifacts & required fields: (please attach to submission)
- Headcount plan: role, level, FTE delta, proposed hire quarter
- Opex items > $5k: vendor, business case, owner, expected term
- Capex requests > $25k: justification and depreciation schedule
- Risk assessment: top 3 risks and mitigation

KPIs & thresholds monitored weekly during close: 
- Net burn vs plan (target variance <10%)
- Gross margin on hosted revenue (target >= 60%)
- Unit token cost vs benchmark (target: < $0.0005/token for mixed workloads)

Approval matrix (budget items):
- <$5k: budget owner approval
- $5k - $50k: Department head + Finance manager
- $50k - $250k: VP + Finance director
- >$250k: CFO + CEO (and Procurement + Legal if vendor contract required)

2) Contracts & Legal Process (commercial contracts):
Purpose: Ensure consistent legal review, standardized commercial terms, and timely execution while controlling legal risk and protecting IP/data.
Required contract types: MSA (Master Services Agreement), Order Form, SOW, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), Security Addendum, Reseller/Partner Agreement.

Contract intake & lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: Sales or Product completes the Contract Intake Form with customer details, proposed term, revenue estimate, special terms (PII, data residency, export controls), and deviation checklist.
2. Pre-legal review (Sales Ops): Validate commercial terms against standard pricebook and discount authority.
3. Legal review: Legal performs risk assessment, proposes redlines. Legal owner: Senior Counsel (owner contact: legal@redwood.com).
4. Security & Privacy review: If customer requires security questionnaire or DPA, routed to Security team for sign-off (SaaS Security Owner: Priya Sharma).
5. Commercial negotiation: Track redlines in contract management system; use standardized clause library.
6. Signature: Execute via DocuSign. Signed contracts uploaded to DocStore and tagged with customer ID, ARR bucket, and confidentiality level.

Turnaround SLAs:
- Standard MSA with no deviations: target 3 business days from intake to legal approval
- Complex deals (custom clauses/data residency): target 10 business days, escalate to GC if beyond 14 days

Contract clauses that trigger mandatory executive review:
- Indemnity cap > $5M or unlimited
- Uncapped liability for IP or security breaches
- Data residency mandates requiring on-prem deployments
- Long-term revenue commitments > $5M or > 36 months

3) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding Procedures:
Purpose: Centralize vendor selection, ensure security/privacy posture, and control spend commitments.
Vendor classification & approval thresholds:
- Low-risk / <$5k annual spend: P-Card or Budget Owner Purchase
- Medium-risk / $5k - $100k: Procurement coordinator + Finance approval + VRA if storing PII
- High-risk / >$100k or strategic vendors: Procurement exec + Legal + Security + CFO approval

Vendor evaluation checklist (required):
- Business need and expected spend (1 - year forecast)
- Vendor legal entity and tax info
- Security posture: SOC2 / ISO27001 / penetration test results or remediation plan
- Data access & processing: PII/PHI? encryption at rest and transit? subprocessor list
- SLA requirements and uptime commitments

Procurement steps:
1. Request: Budget owner submits Purchase Request (PR) with vendor, scope, term, and associated budget line.
2. VRA & Security review: Security team completes vendor questionnaire for any vendor accessing customer data or internal systems.
3. Negotiation & Contracting: Legal reviews vendor contract; standard procurement addendum applied.
4. PO issuance & payment terms: Finance issues PO and sets payment term (default Net 30 for non-enterprise vendors).
5. Onboarding & inventory: Procurement records vendor in Vendor Registry and tracks contract expiry and renewal reminders.

Payment terms & exceptions:
- Standard: Net 30 from invoice date
- Prepay or net 0: require VP Finance approval and justification
- Statement of Work with milestone payments: require escrow of deliverables and acceptance criteria in SOW

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies:
Purpose: Ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606 principles and that invoicing is timely, auditable, and consistent across product lines.
Revenue streams and recognition patterns:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue over time as usage occurs. Invoices generated monthly in arrears; unbilled revenue recognized when usage is reported but invoiced later.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): For committed reservations sold prepaid or billed monthly, recognize revenue over the reservation term. If customer prepays, record as deferred revenue and amortize over term.
- Private deployments (licenses + services): 
  - Software license component: typically recognized over time if significant customization / continuous access, otherwise evaluate as point-in-time if perpetual license.
  - Professional services: recognized based on milestone completion or percentage of completion if criteria met.

Billing cadence & terms:
- Standard customer billing: Monthly in arrears for usage-based Hosted API; invoice due Net 30.
- Enterprise invoicing: Can be monthly or quarterly in arrears; payment terms negotiated (Net 30 default; Net 45/60 require CFO approval).
- Reserved capacity: invoiced per contract (monthly, quarterly, or annual). Prepaid reservations recorded as contract liabilities.

Credits, refunds & disputes:
- Credits for outages: Apply per SLA defined in executed contract. Any credit > $10k requires Finance + Legal approval.
- Billing dispute process: Customer must notify within 60 days of invoice; disputes logged in billing tracker and paused for collection until resolution.
- Refunds: Rare; disallowed for consumption already delivered unless material error is confirmed by Finance.

Revenue accounting controls & close checklist (monthly close):
- Reconcile billing ledger to usage records (token-level reconciliation sample)
- Review deferred revenue roll-forward and amortization schedules
- Confirm contract modifications and change orders (documented in contract repository)
- Verify unbilled receivables and cut-off for month-end
- Ensure any credits/refunds > $5k have documented approval

Internal roles & ownership (summary):
- FP&A / Finance: budgeting, forecasts, billing operations, month-end close (owner: Maria Lopez)
- Legal: contract review, clause library, escalations (owner: Owen Li)
- Security: vendor security reviews, DPAs, contract security addenda (owner: Priya Sharma)
- Procurement Coordinator: vendor onboarding, POs, vendor registry (owner: Dave Chen)
- Sales Ops: contract intake & pricebook validation (owner: Lauren Kim)

Escalation & exceptions process:
- If a procurement, contract, or revenue event falls outside playbook thresholds, submit an Exceptions Request with justification to finance-legal-exceptions@redwood.com. Include business case, estimated financial impact, and mitigation plan.
- Exceptions > $1M or with significant legal risk require GC and CFO approval.

Appendix A - Approval matrices (quick reference):
- Procurement: see Procurement thresholds above (P-Card, Manager, VP, CFO)
- Contracts: Standard deviations and signatory authority table: 
  - Standard MSA & order forms: Sales Director up to $250k ARR
  - Custom MSA or term >36 months or >$5M ARR: require GC + CFO

Appendix B - Contract checklist (before signature):
- Verify counterparty legal name and signatory authority
- Confirm SOW deliverables, acceptance criteria, and payment milestones
- Security & privacy clauses present (DPA if processing customer data)
- SLA & remedies defined (SLA credits capped per contract)
- Export control and sanctions check completed

Appendix C - Sample SOW clause snippet (legal library):
"""
Acceptance Criteria: Customer will have 10 business days from delivery to validate deliverables. Acceptance occurs when Customer provides written notice or fails to provide rejection within 10 business days. Acceptance occurs when Customer provides written notice or fails to provide rejection within 10 business days. Payments tied to acceptance milestones are due Net 30 following acceptance.
"""

Document maintenance and review:
- This playbook is owned by Finance (FP&A) and Legal. It will be reviewed annually in Q4 and updated as required for new product offerings or accounting guidance changes.

Questions & contacts:
- Finance general: finance@redwood.com
- Contracts & Legal: legal@redwood.com
- Procurement & Vendor Registry: procurement@redwood.com
- Billing ops: billing@redwood.com
